title: Formulary Benefit Clinical Pharmacy Criteria: Recent Denials and the Length of a Non-Formulary Approval
content:
**Criterion.** Under the Formulary Benefit, a recent-denial shortening is applied to a standard non-formulary exception approval when the drug was refused for the member within the denial lookback of **12** months. A denial is within the lookback when it was recorded fewer whole months than 12 before the decision date. The member's exception history for the drug is read, including the reason recorded on each denial.

| Denials of the drug within the lookback | Taken off the approval period |
|---|---|
| at least one recorded for alternatives not tried | **3** months |
| one or more for any other reason, none for alternatives not tried | **1** month |
| none | nothing |

The shortening is taken off the approval period before the floor of one month is applied. The two amounts are never both taken off: an alternatives-not-tried denial in the lookback decides the shortening at 3 months.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical decision date of 15 September)

- A missing-prescriber-statement denial dated 2 February, which is 7 whole months back, takes off 1 month.
- An alternatives-not-tried denial dated 16 September of the previous year, which is 11 whole months back, takes off 3 months.
- An alternatives-not-tried denial dated 15 September of the previous year, which is 12 whole months back, is outside the lookback and takes off nothing.
